evidence_use.operator: per-visit arithmetic mean, sample SD, nonmissing count
evidence_use.population: 75 adults with overweight or obesity; 12-week internet behavioral weight-management program, then 9 months without additional intervention; measurements at months 0,3,6,9,12.
evidence_use.measurement: Clinic weight in kg; PFS total average of 15 1-5 items; No-Go errors integer; delay-discounting AUC separately for $100 and $1000 conditions.
evidence_use.provenance: source_packet_A; supplied target-derived marginals, reconstruction regime A0
evidence_use.reason: Use all 25 outcome-visit means and sample SDs to parameterize marginal distributions, and all 25 nonmissing counts exactly at n=75. Stratified quantiles stabilize finite-sample margins. These target-derived summaries are construction inputs, not independent validation. Marginal shapes, all joint associations, and individual missingness remain unidentified. Moment estimates are used as distribution parameters; exact finite-sample moment equality is not claimed. The same generated observed-value multiset is paired across scenarios for each fixed seed; changing assignments and masks cannot independently validate joint dependence.

evidence_use.population: 75 adults with overweight or obesity; 12-week internet behavioral weight-management program, then 9 months without additional intervention; measurements at months 0,3,6,9,12.
evidence_use.measurement: Clinic weight in kg; PFS total average of 15 1-5 items; No-Go errors integer; delay-discounting AUC separately for $100 and $1000 conditions.
evidence_use.reason: Generate five visits per new synthetic person, positive weight, a baseline-only weight limit of 180 kg, PFS on the 1/15 measurement lattice within 1-5, integer No-Go errors within 0-512, and discounting AUC in 0-1. Eligibility describes the intended population; age, BMI, pregnancy and contraindications cannot be represented or verified because their component measurements are outside this bounded schema.

components.name: outcome-specific marginal distributions
components.source_to_target_assumptions: Same-population A0 reconstruction. Weight uses a lognormal distribution with baseline upper truncation; PFS uses a scaled beta rounded to a 1/15 lattice; No-Go errors use an overdispersed negative binomial truncated at 512; each discounting condition uses beta margins. Sample SDs parameterize distribution SDs before truncation/rounding. Each observed margin has independently jittered stratified quantiles assigned according to latent ranks. These choices favor valid support and source-compatible moments but assume unreported distribution shapes and suppress unconditional sampling variation of the margins.

components.name: three latent joint structures
components.source_to_target_assumptions: Variable order is weight_kg, pfs, gng, dd100, dd1000. The target anchor preserves parent Gaussian person-factor and occasion-factor correlations: discounting-only off-diagonal entries 0.70 and 0.50, and repeatabilities [0.94,0.60,0.50,0.65,0.65]. shared_trait adds loadings L=[0.45,0.65,0.45,-0.45,-0.45] to person correlation: LL^T + diag(sqrt(1-L^2)) R_person diag(sqrt(1-L^2)). Its occasion factors and repeatabilities remain unchanged. state_selection applies the same factor construction to occasion correlation, preserves parent person correlation, sets repeatabilities [0.75,0.30,0.25,0.35,0.35], and imposes occasion AR(1)=0.40 between adjacent scheduled visits. These are positive-semidefinite working constructions; numeric values and directions are not source-estimated and observed-scale correlations are not those latent parameters.

components.name: exact counts and observation-rank assignment
components.source_to_target_assumptions: Every outcome/visit observed count is round(source_n_observed*n/75). target and shared_trait retain outcome-independent availability-score variance fractions 0.60 person, 0.30 visit, 0.10 endpoint. state_selection uses sqrt(1-0.45^2)*that_score + 0.45*baseline_behavior_score, where the latter is the unit-variance latent contrast pfs+gng-dd100-dd1000 computed from known latent covariance. Lower missing-score ranks are observed. Thus larger baseline PFS/No-Go and lower baseline AUC make later missingness more likely, by assumption. Baseline remains fully observed. No dependence on unobserved future realized outcomes is claimed. Missingness can be intermittent. Exact observed margins are conditionally rebuilt after selection; this is not an identified complete-data selection model.

components.name: paired source-conditioned margins and fresh keys
components.source_to_target_assumptions: Identical random-number array sizes and stratified-quantile streams across contexts give identical observed marginal multisets at a fixed seed while changing person/visit ranks and masks. New within-cohort numeric IDs identify synthetic persons only. General-n counts use source sample size from evidence; small-n finite sample SDs need not approximate source SDs. No patient records, file I/O, global RNG mutation, or evidence changes occur inside generate.

scenarios.assumption: Parent anchor: stable but mutually independent weight/PFS/No-Go domains, a shared discounting domain, and outcome-independent shared attendance. Numerical repeatability and discounting correlations are inherited working assumptions.
scenarios.inclusion_rationale: Keep the valid parent construction as an interpretable separate-domain anchor. Missing covariance does not establish independence, so it is one retained assumption rather than a definitive reconstruction.

scenarios.assumption: A stable common individual trait raises weight/PFS/No-Go ranks and lowers both discounting AUC ranks, with independent-of-outcome observation scores. Explicit signed loadings are a sensitivity hypothesis; no biological or clinical finding is asserted.
scenarios.inclusion_rationale: A persistent shared individual propensity is scientifically distinct from separate domains and can alter baseline associations and longitudinal weight associations while honoring exactly the same supplied marginal evidence. It is not a seed variation.

scenarios.assumption: Most cross-domain coupling acts through a changing shared occasion state with lag decay and lower persistent variance; higher baseline behavioral contrast also predicts later missingness. Trait and changing-state hypotheses are alternatives, not fitted claims.
scenarios.inclusion_rationale: A transient shared state with baseline-related attendance is another evidence-compatible process. It interrogates trajectory covariance misspecification and informative composition of observed follow-up samples. Its changes are bundled as a process scenario, so differences cannot be attributed uniquely to one parameter.

changes_from_parent.parent_joint_review: The parent successfully satisfies source contracts but assumes unreported cross-domain independence and outcome-independent availability. Marginal compatibility cannot select these restrictions. A bounded three-scenario set is warranted because unresolved joint dependence materially affects all three declared analysis classes.
